title: The members of his 1947 group who waited for him
summary: Cobb lists his band: Dave Page, Booty Wood, Charlie Fowlkes, George Rhodes, Walter Buchanan and Jumping George Jones, all of whom returned when he recovered.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who were the guys you were gonna take out?
Who were the guys who ... what?
Who were the guys you were gonna take out on the road?
That was in my group? The trumpet player

was Dave Page, the trombone player was Michael Wood^A and Charlie Fowlkes Folsom was the baritone saxophone player, who is with Basie now. And myself, as the front line, the four horns. George Rhodes, who is Sammy Davis Jr.'s conductor today, was on piano; Walter Buchanan on bass, and Poor Jumping George Jones on drums. That was my group.

Now this is what I had done. When I had my operation, I told them, going in for this operation, "When I come back, if I come back out, the first preference is for you, wherever you may be, and I will send you a notice when I get ready to start back again, if I start back again. I don't know." And I sent every one of them a notice, and do you know, every one of them came back with me when I got up out of bed? Booty was with Erskine Hawkins; he listened to me. George Rhodes was with someone where else, but he came back. But everybody -- because I know they got to work.

But we enjoyed one another as a family band, and everybody loved one another. But I said, "Now, if you got something else to do, then I've got to get somebody else." Every one of them came back, Helen.
